messages:
support_jess: FYI we have a customer (Alan / acme-inc) complaining about elevated 5xxs and latency since 09:12 UTC. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~8% on hosted API. Traces show gateway 502/504. sample log: "upstream response timeout; auth-proxy: EOF while reading header". attaching trace ids: trace/abc123

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: canary rollout region-routing-v2@prod at 09:10 by matt. Canary weight: 10%

elaine: oncall — can someone confirm what changed in region-routing-v2? Any flag flips or sidecar config swaps?

matt: I flipped region_routing_v2 from 0 -> 10% at 09:09 as part of release 2026-03-17. No other infra changes. I see the 502 spike correlating with the rollout.

samir: digging into auth-proxy logs — seeing header truncation when requests route to the new variant. Example log line:
```
2026-03-17T09:12:24Z auth-proxy ERROR request_id=abc123 upstream EOF reading header: "Authorization" truncated (len 64 -> 32)
```
I suspect the region variant includes a sidecar config that changed proxy buffer sizing.

engineering_oncall: can you paste the proxy/nginx snippet for the region variant? grep for proxy_buffer_size or buffers.

samir: snippet from the diff:
```
proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;
proxy_buffer_size 32k;
proxy_buffers 4 32k;
# region_routing_v2 uses sidecar buffer patch that accidentally sets proxy_buffer_size=32 (bytes)
```

matt: oh crap — the diff comment is accurate. The new patch set proxy_buffer_size=32 (missing 'k'). That makes the header buffer tiny and will truncate auth headers. That would explain the EOF / 502.

elaine: assign rollback. @matt please flip the flag back to 0 and abort the canary. @support_jess notify Alan we're rolling back.

matt: rolling back flag now. curl -XPOST https://console.internal/api/flags/region_routing_v2 -d '{"weight":0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'

deploy-bot: Rollout updated: region_routing_v2 weight -> 0% by matt at 09:18. Canary aborted.

sre-bot: metric alert: 5xx rate returning to baseline within 2m after rollback. latency normalized. :white_check_mark:

support_jess: Updated Alan: "We rolled the canary back and are investigating root cause; we'll follow up with a timeline." He asked for ETA on a permanent fix.

samir: plan: revert buffer size change to include units, add unit test + e2e that sends long Authorization header to canary, and a canary gating check to fail pre-rollout if header gets truncated. I'll open a PR now.

engineering_oncall: also add a predeploy smoke test that runs a long-header request against the canary sidecar for every region change.

matt: created PR #1287 with fix and tests (includes corrected buffer size and header-length test). Will re-run canary at 1% and ramp slowly after green tests.

elaine: good. Owners: samir (fix + tests), matt (deploy + canary), support_jess (customer comms). Add postmortem and CS note. Target: follow-up doc in 24h.

support_jess: noted. I'll coordinate CS note and billing review — Alan reported elevated billing due to retries; finance to check impact.

samir: quick postmortem note: root cause = human error in sidecar config (missing unit on buffer size). Mitigation: stricter config linting, header-length smoke test, canary gating.

matt: thanks all. I'll paste links to PR and canary results when available and reopen if issues.

customer_alan: thanks for the quick rollback. Please confirm once the fix and safe canary are in so we can resume normal traffic.

elaine: will update here once PR merges and canary passes. :v:
